newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Quebrada Blanca union confirms strike vote.
newsitem.headline: Chile Quebrada Blanca union confirms strike vote.

text.p: Miners at the Quebrada Blance copper mine have voted overwhemingly to reject the company's final pay offer and go on strike on Wednesday, said union leader Juan Madariaga.
Of the 302 workers who voted, 300 were in favor of strike action with only two accepting the pay deal, Madariaga told Reuters by telephone from Iquique.
The strike is due to start from first shift Wednesday.
Management had offered a one percent pay increase in real terms -- the union had demanded 18 percent.
Vancouver-based Cominco Ltd, Cominco Resources and Teck Resources International hold a 76.5 percent stake in Quebrada Blanca.
The mine, which lies close to the border with Bolivia, produces 75,000 tonnes of copper cathodes a year.
The stoppage will be the second in Chile's all-important copper mining industry this month. A small group of workers at the giant Escondida pit walked out over a week ago after wage talks broke down.
